name: Prisoner's Dilemma
note: Both players prefer mutual cooperation (3,3), but each has a dominant strategy to defect, so they end at (2,2), their second-worst outcome.

name: Patron
binomialName: Prisoner's Dilemma × Battle of the Sexes

name: Chicken
note: Hawk–Dove. Mutual Hawk is the worst outcome for both (1,1); mutual Dove gives both second-best (3,3). The two equilibria are very unequal: one swerves, one doesn't.

name: Patron
binomialName: Battle of the Sexes × Prisoner's Dilemma

name: Battle of the Sexes
note: A couple wants to do something together, but each has a different first choice. Two equilibria, each favouring one player.

name: Protector
binomialName: Battle of the Sexes × Prisoner's Delight

name: Hero
note: A Battle-type game with two equilibria, each giving one player their best outcome and the other their second-best.

name: Protector
binomialName: Prisoner's Delight × Battle of the Sexes

name: Prisoner's Delight
note: Called Anti-Chicken on the chart. Dominant strategies lead both players to their second-best outcome (3,3).

name: Deadlock
note: Called Anti-Prisoner's Dilemma on the chart. Incentives lead to the second-best outcome (3,3) for both.

name: Samson
binomialName: No Conflict × Battle of the Sexes

name: Blackmail Type
note: A Jekyll-Hyde type game: incentives make one player kind and the other cruel.

name: Asymmetric Prisoner's Dilemma
note: One high swap from Prisoner's Dilemma; a second high swap for the other player turns it into Stag Hunt.

name: Inspector
binomialName: Stag Hunt × Battle of the Sexes

name: Fixed Sum
note: Ordinal equivalent of zero-sum: gains for one are losses for the other. Cyclic, since one player always wants to move; maximin strategies avoid the worst payoff.

name: Generous
binomialName: Mixed Harmony × Battle of the Sexes

name: Samaritan's Dilemma
note: One player could do fine alone; the other wants to help whatever happens, while the helped player most prefers to be helped and do less.

name: No Conflict
note: The best outcomes coincide and dominant strategies lead straight there.

name: Stag Hunt
note: Cooperating on the stag gives both their best outcome; hunting hare is the safe choice. Two equilibria: (4,4) and (2,2).

name: Assurance
note: Two equilibria, but both players prefer the same one (4,4); the risk is failing to coordinate on it.

name: Coordination
note: Pure coordination problem: two equilibria, with both preferring (4,4) over (3,3).

name: Mixed Harmony
note: Interests mostly aligned; dominant strategies lead to win-win (4,4).

name: Harmony
note: Either player's choice benefits the other, and incentives lead to win-win (4,4).

name: Asymmetric Prisoner's Dilemma
note: One high swap from Prisoner's Dilemma; a second high swap for the other player turns it into Stag Hunt.
